note: Durable resolution state for audit findings. reconcileFindings() (lib/findingsRegister.mjs) matches new audit output by fingerprint = file+symbol+discriminator, so a distinct issue in the same symbol never collapses into a prior entry and can never be silently suppressed. A FIXED entry is only trustworthy with a regressionTest; entries were verified by reading current code at verifiedAtCommit.

entries.evidence: FIXED (register was stale at KNOWN_ACCEPTED): functions/src/inventoryService.ts now claims (workOrderId,state) atomically via claimStateForProcessing() inside db().runTransaction, mirroring the reservationLockRef pattern, so a crash between the ledger write and the processed marker can no longer re-run trigger() and duplicate entries. Landed by #932 (54e11b59, site-work r3 N) with 28 lines of new test coverage.

Proven by functions/test/workOrderAvailability.test.mjs (5 tests: double-booking rejected; terminal/pre-dispatch free; self-redispatch and other-tech allowed).

entries.evidence: Verified open at this commit: the component defines getDerivedStateFromError and componentDidCatch but contains zero reset/retry/remount wiring (grep for reset|retry returns 0). Any single render crash latches the fallback for the remainder of the session with no user-recoverable path -- the whole app is dead until a manual reload.

Verified open: getAvailableQuantity sums only RESERVED/RELEASED against the static catalog baseline and contains no reference to RECEIVED/TRANSFER_IN/TRANSFER_OUT (0 matches in the function body), while receiveInventoryStockCommand stages those types into the same inventory_transactions collection. Dormant only because the receiving capability is registered-but-ungranted; it will activate silently on grant, with received stock never affecting reservation availability.

Verified open: assignJob is still exported with zero live call sites, yet firestore.rules fieldops_jobs still authorizes the update unconditionally for admin/dispatcher. Unlike the governed fieldops_wos path it is a bare client runTransaction with no audit event and no idempotency key, so a direct console call (or any future rewiring) reintroduces unaudited dual-write authority over assignment.

Verified open: the file header still asserts Production Rules DENY the equipment collection outright, while firestore.rules already grants create/update to isAdminOrDispatcher() with shape/ownership/transition validation. Not an active vulnerability -- the Rules boundary is sound -- but anyone assessing blast radius from this comment will wrongly believe Equipment writes are blocked at the database layer.

Verified open: signature is canTransitionJob(currentStatus, nextStatus) -- no role parameter -- so it permits in_progress->complete for any caller, while firestore.rules reserves technician completion for the trusted completeAssignedJob callable. Fails closed today only because updateJobStatus has no live UI call site; wiring it into technician-facing Field Mode would ship a button whose only defence is a mid-transaction permission-denied.
